tEn: The Programmable Data Center: Evan Conrad of SF Compute
tZh: 可编程数据中心：对话 SF Compute 的 Evan Conrad
sEn: Evan Conrad of SF Compute explains how physical settlement and a purpose-built order book turn compute into a tradable market.
sZh: SF Compute 的 Evan Conrad 讲述如何通过实物交割与专用订单簿，把算力变成可交易的市场。

consensus.en: Physical settlement is essential for a credible compute market; financialization must follow, not precede it.
consensus.zh: 实物交割是可信算力市场的基础；金融化必须在其后，而非之前。

consensus.en: Compute is not fungible; many dimensions like chip generation, storage, and interruption terms matter.
consensus.zh: 算力并非同质化；芯片代际、存储、中断条款等众多维度都重要。

consensus.en: The compute forward curve is humped: near-term unsold capacity drops in price, then rises, then declines.
consensus.zh: 算力远期曲线呈驼峰状：近期未售出容量价格下跌，随后上升，再下降。

consensus.en: Current B300 inference revenue (~$40/hr) far exceeds rental cost (~$5-6/hr); one must adjust.
consensus.zh: 当前B300推理收入（约$40/小时）远超租赁成本（约$5-6/小时）；两者必有一变。

consensus.en: SF Compute must stay independent (not own hardware) to avoid manipulating the forwards market.
consensus.zh: SF Compute必须保持独立（不拥有硬件），以避免操纵远期市场。

consensus.en: Standardizing compute contracts is far off; first make operations uniform, then standardize.
consensus.zh: 算力合约标准化尚远；先统一运营，再标准化。

contrarian.en: Nvidia can't build a compute exchange because it wouldn't be independent enough for trading.
contrarian.zh: 英伟达无法建立算力交易所，因为它不够独立，难以用于交易。

contrarian.en: Hyperscalers and cloud providers can't run this market; they'd have to kill their core business.
contrarian.zh: 超大规模云厂商无法运营此市场；他们必须扼杀核心业务才能做到。

contrarian.en: Cash-settled futures before physical settlement create manipulable markets with high basis risk.
contrarian.zh: 在实物交割前推出现金结算期货会制造可操纵市场和高基差风险。

contrarian.en: Compute prices may be higher in the future even if spot is low, due to lock-in demand.
contrarian.zh: 尽管现货价格低，但由于锁定需求，未来算力价格可能更高。

contrarian.en: Early GPU cohorts (H100, GB200) had firmware bugs; sophisticated buyers pay more for later batches.
contrarian.zh: 早期GPU批次（H100、GB200）存在固件缺陷；成熟买家愿为后期批次支付溢价。

turns.zh: 是的。所以我们已经能够把问题减少到一定程度。

turns.en: Okay. Interesting. All right. So, I think that's like a lot of nitty-gritty. turns.en: Mainly just the requirement for physical settlement. We think that if you—we spent 3 years learning why you need physical settlement. turns.zh: 主要是实物结算的要求。我们认为如果你——我们花了 3 年时间学习为什么需要实物结算。而我们今天整个对话就是，这些东西并不像你想象的那么可替代。我们将尝试使它们可替代。这是行业的工作。但如果没有这一点，你会面临很多风险。

turns.en: If you try to build too much financialization before the industry has had time to build out the physical settlement, then I think what you have is a market that's very easy to manipulate and a market that has a lot of basis risk, where the price you may be hedging against actually has nothing to do with the price that you can actually buy the capacity for.
turns.zh: 如果你在行业还没来得及建立实物结算之前就试图过度金融化，那么我认为你会得到一个非常容易被操纵的市场，以及一个存在大量基差风险的市场，你用来对冲的价格实际上与你真正能买到的产能价格毫无关系。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yeah.

turns.zh: 所以对于听众来说，我们上次简要谈过这个，但人们常常震惊地发现，比如说，信用违约互换的市场规模是其保险债券的 12 倍。类似这样，或者像抵押贷款再保险的市场等等——它比标的实物结算要大。所以这就是实物结算与现金结算的区别。

turns.en: Yeah. And basically cash settlements are exactly the kind of side bet that you see in The Big Short, where they may or may not have anything to do with the underlying thing itself, and it may be used as a proxy for overall other stuff. And you don't want that to go out of control.
turns.zh: 是的。基本上，现金结算正是你在《大空头》中看到的那种旁注，它们可能与标的物本身有关，也可能无关，并且可能被用作其他整体事物的代理。你不希望这种情况失控。

turns.en: Yes. Yeah. So, to be clear, we think cash settlement as a future concept is a great idea. We just think it should be derived from physical settlement. Because, as you said, it's a side bet, and it would be kind of like if you made a cash settlement future before you made physical settlement.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。所以，明确地说，我们认为现金结算作为一个未来概念是个好主意。我们只是认为它应该从实物结算中衍生出来。因为，正如你所说，它是一种旁注，这有点像你在做实物结算之前就做了现金结算期货。

turns.en: Which I think people are kind of doing already.
turns.zh: 我认为人们已经在某种程度上这样做了。

turns.en: Not yet, totally. People are trying to make cash settlement before you make the physical settlement.
turns.zh: 还没有完全。人们试图在实物结算之前就进行现金结算。

turns.en: Do that for all sorts of things, including startup stock.
turns.zh: 对各种东西都这样做，包括初创公司股票。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Right? Like you can buy and sell a made-up share of OpenAI, but it's nothing to do with the actual share.
turns.zh: 对吧？就像你可以买卖一个虚构的 OpenAI 股份，但它与实际股份无关。

turns.en: Yes. And lots of those go very poorly. Like it would be kind of bad if you made a—it would be bad if you started selling the derivative on a stock that doesn't exist yet.
turns.zh: 是的。而且很多这样的交易结果很糟糕。就像如果你做了一个——如果你开始对一个还不存在的股票出售衍生品，那会很糟糕。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。

turns.en: Well, so, I mean, one thing that we do—so I used to be a currency trader, right? And interest rates as well. turns.zh: 那么，我的意思是，我们做的一件事——所以我曾经是一名货币交易员，对吧？还有利率。我们做的一件事是，有一个董事会聚集在一起说，这是伦敦银行同业拆借利率，LIBOR，我们都同意这是每月定盘价，我们都按照那个定盘价交易。这在 3 年后的某个时候还有意义吗？

turns.zh: 我们目前的担忧是——

That's what we're concerned about.
turns.zh: 是的。嗯，我们的担忧是存在一个非常相似的问题，你可以操纵一个指数。我们的印象是，为什么你可以操纵那个指数，是因为很多指数基于非常少量的数据，而这些数据与购买新储备合同的实际价格没有太大相关性。这就是我们所担心的。

turns.zh: 好的。有趣。好吧。我认为这就是大致的情况。我想今天的另一部分是你与 Oliver 交谈过，你正在与 Jump 举办活动，并且你与 Silicon Data 是朋友。你从所有这些其他参与者那里学到了什么？比如你想指出哪些主要参与者正在做有趣的事情？

turns.en: Ooh. So, we're big fans of Silicon Data and Computer Change. I think they were also very early to this, and I think they are doing a reasonable shot at the A path that we think that we'll likely end up being partners with.
turns.zh: 哦。所以，我们是 Silicon Data 和 Computer Change 的忠实粉丝。我认为他们也很早进入这个领域，我认为他们在 A 路径上做出了合理的尝试，我们认为我们最终可能会成为合作伙伴。

turns.en: And can you distinguish like your different paths?
turns.zh: 你能区分一下你们不同的路径吗？

turns.en: So, the general gist is they're doing cash settlement, we're doing physical settlement. We think both can exist and should exist, and that they're sort of mutually beneficial to each other. And so, totally fine. So, I think they are one of the earliest in the space, and I think they very clearly took the bet well before anybody else did, and I think that's very honorable to do.
turns.zh: 所以，大体上是他们做现金结算，我们做实物结算。我们认为两者都可以存在，也应该存在，并且它们彼此互利。所以，完全没问题。所以，我认为他们是这个领域最早的之一，我认为他们显然比任何人都更早下了赌注，我认为这非常值得尊敬。

turns.en: You mentioned John Seminalysis says Jump. Like are these other players emerging like as far—like you were my first introduction to this, and then I see all these other guys coming in, and I'm like, 'Okay, something's happening here.' I don't know the landscape as clearly as you do.
turns.zh: 你提到了 John Seminalysis 说 Jump。这些其他参与者是否也在涌现——就像你是我第一次接触这个，然后我看到所有这些人进来，我想，‘好吧，这里正在发生一些事情。’我不像你那样清楚地了解这个领域。

turns.en: Yeah, so the categories of folks that we've seen is there's folks that are trying to set better standards. So, Seminalysis I think is working to try and create better standards. There's folks that are trying to do residual value insurance and so on. There's a number of different companies in the space. I don't know any of them super well, but I know this is a concept, and I think that's important. There are folks that are trying to do deposit lending where they'll front your credit risk for the cloud. There's an ecosystem of companies that are forming around how do we resolve the financial bottlenecks of compute, and it is cool to see.
turns.zh: 是的，所以我们看到的类别是，有些人试图制定更好的标准。所以，我认为 Seminalysis 正在努力创建更好的标准。有些人试图做残值保险等等。这个领域有许多不同的公司。我对它们都不是很了解，但我知道这是一个概念，我认为这很重要。有些人试图做存款贷款，他们将为云提供信用风险。有一个公司生态系统正在围绕如何解决计算的财务瓶颈形成，这很酷。

turns.en: I think effectively what you want in this ecosystem is buyers and sellers, you want an analyst, you want—we said insurance or what's the—
turns.zh: 我认为在这个生态系统中，你有效需要的是买家和卖家，你需要一个分析师，你需要——我们说过保险还是什么——

turns.en: Uh residual value insurance.
turns.zh: 呃，残值保险。

turns.en: Residual. Um, and you want this like healthy ecosystem out there. But you obviously you guys are owning the problem of physical settlement, which is really interesting. Okay, so I mean, we can go into like the hard tech side because obviously you are also hiring for extremely cracked engineers. Describe your stack.
turns.zh: 残值。嗯，你希望有一个健康的生态系统。但显然你们正在解决实物结算的问题，这真的很有趣。好的，所以我的意思是，我们可以进入硬科技方面，因为显然你们也在招聘极其顶尖的工程师。描述一下你们的技术栈。

turns.en: We do all the things the cloud does without being the cloud. As in we don't own the hardware. The reason why we don't own the hardware is because if we did, we would be able to manipulate the forwards market. So, we have to be Switzerland, we have to be independent, which creates a lot of sort of strange things about the company, but in order to do physical settlement, you have to do site visits. You have to visit the data center. You have to design the bill of materials and ensure that—you have to basically do like supply chain consulting, where you have relationships with different OEMs that ensure that things get delivered on time. Then you have to do cluster architecture, so you're sort of designing the cluster itself. Then you're rolling out racks or you're working with partners to roll out racks and then supervising that.
turns.zh: 我们做云做的所有事情，但不是云。也就是说，我们不拥有硬件。我们不拥有硬件的原因是因为如果我们拥有，我们就能操纵远期市场。所以，我们必须保持中立，必须独立，这给公司带来了很多奇怪的事情，但为了进行实物结算，你必须进行实地考察。你必须参观数据中心。你必须设计物料清单并确保——你必须基本上做供应链咨询，与不同的 OEM 建立关系，确保按时交付。然后你必须做集群架构，所以你在设计集群本身。然后你部署机架，或者与合作伙伴一起部署机架，然后监督。

transcript.sec: Backplane Management and Data Center Operations

turns.en: Then you're doing backplane management, so you're taking over the PDUs and the switches and the DPUs and UFM and BMC and the operating harness around the nodes that you're settling.
turns.zh: 然后你们做背板管理，所以你们接管了 PDU、交换机、DPU、UFM 和 BMC，以及围绕你们所部署节点的运营框架。

turns.en: You as an SF Compute employee?
turns.zh: 你作为 SF Compute 的员工？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: All right. So when you buy a node from a cloud, there's the bare metal, but there's all this around the bare metal. And in order to make that bare metal node work, you have to operate everything else.
turns.zh: 好吧。所以当你从云提供商那里购买一个节点时，有裸金属，但裸金属周围还有一大堆东西。为了让那个裸金属节点工作，你必须运营其他所有东西。

turns.en: Because I just like traditionally the job of the data center is to extract some of this away from you.
turns.zh: 因为传统上数据中心的工作就是帮你把其中一些东西抽离出来。

turns.en: Yeah. We're the ones that do that.
turns.zh: 是的。我们就是做这个的。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. Okay, all right. But you're not in the data center business. You're not the Equinixes of the world.
turns.zh: 对对。好的，明白了。但你们不在数据中心业务里。你们不是像 Equinix 那样的公司。

turns.en: We're not in the data center business, sort of. What we do work with is—so, we offer supercomputing as a service. And what this means is folks come to us and say, you know, I've got X, where X is I've got X megawatts here, and maybe sometimes they mean, I've got a data center that I would like to turn into a GPU cluster. Like my options are I could sell the GPU cluster or I could sell the data center to somebody or I could become the cloud. And then we go to them and say, great, we will turn you into the cloud, we're the supercomputing part, you're the data center cloud. Let's partner together and then we will sell and all make money. Sometimes it's people who have something that could turn into a data center, in which case we're going to basically project manage that up to the layer, and then we will work with those folks to turn their powered land or whatever they have into a data center by working with partners, and then we take over at the supercomputing part. This requires us to have some sort of data center expertise in-house, but we don't self-perform builds. So yeah.
turns.zh: 我们不算是在数据中心业务里。我们做的是——我们提供超级计算即服务。这意味着人们来找我们说，你知道，我有 X，X 就是我有 X 兆瓦，有时他们的意思是，我有一个数据中心，我想把它变成 GPU 集群。我的选择是，我可以卖掉 GPU 集群，或者把数据中心卖给别人，或者我自己成为云。然后我们去找他们说，太好了，我们会把你变成云，我们是超级计算部分，你是数据中心云。我们合作，然后我们一起销售，一起赚钱。有时是那些拥有可以变成数据中心的东西的人，在这种情况下，我们基本上会项目管理到那个层面，然后我们会与那些人合作，通过合作伙伴将他们有电力的土地或任何他们拥有的东西变成数据中心，然后我们在超级计算部分接手。这要求我们在内部拥有某种数据中心专业知识，但我们不自行建造。所以是的。

turns.en: Yeah, so it's somewhat modular because you have different scenarios you need to deploy under.
turns.zh: 是的，所以这有点模块化，因为你们需要在不同的场景下部署。

turns.en: Yeah, someone once described us as like Palantir for compute because it's like these each time it's this new rodeo, but we deeply partner with folks on both sides.
turns.zh: 是的，有人曾把我们描述为计算领域的 Palantir，因为每次都是新的挑战，但我们与双方的人都深度合作。

turns.en: Yeah. And primarily the US?
turns.zh: 是的。主要在美国？

turns.en: Primarily the US, but we operate around the world.
turns.zh: 主要在美国，但我们在全球运营。

turns.en: Yeah. At some point does SF Compute become a misnomer?
turns.zh: 是的。到了某个时候，SF Compute 会不会变成一个误称？

turns.en: So, we're deploying clusters all around the world, and when we do that, we're working with people who themselves are trying to be clouds all around the world. They look like sovereign compute players. And our pitch to sovereign compute is amazing. Let's help you set up a cloud in your own country and we will bring the San Francisco off-take. We'll bring the San Francisco expertise. We'll set up the clusters. That's our whole business. We're going to make it financeable.
turns.zh: 所以，我们正在全球部署集群，当我们这样做时，我们与那些自己也想成为云的人合作。他们看起来像主权计算参与者。我们对主权计算的推销很棒。让我们帮助你在自己的国家建立云，我们将带来旧金山的承购。我们将带来旧金山的专业知识。我们将建立集群。这就是我们的全部业务。我们将使其可融资。

turns.en: Ah. Who are your main biggest announced partners that you can name?
turns.zh: 啊。你能说出你们宣布的主要最大合作伙伴吗？

turns.en: Nobody I can name basically. We will have some announcements in a week or two that we expect to come on.
turns.zh: 基本上没有我能说的。我们预计在一两周内会有一些公告。

turns.en: Yeah. All things sort of uh—Sure, sure. Good luck. Yeah. No, I mean I think this is really interesting for every country to like who's investing in sovereign AI to figure this out and it's interesting that like SF is still sort of like that brand name and that is very marketable.
turns.zh: 是的。所有事情有点——当然，当然。祝好运。是的。不，我的意思是，我认为这对每个国家来说都非常有趣，比如谁在投资主权 AI 来解决这个问题，有趣的是，SF 仍然有点像那个品牌名称，而且非常有市场价值。

turns.en: So I think one of the interesting things is just thinking through this market.
turns.zh: 所以我认为有趣的事情之一就是思考这个市场。

turns.en: Mhm. Nvidia is obviously like the 800-lb gorilla in the room. Why don't they—Why didn't they make SF Compute? And again like I you know, the answer's going to be market manipulation but like let's just really get into the incentives of the multiple players.
turns.zh: 嗯。英伟达显然是房间里的大猩猩。他们为什么不——为什么他们没有做出 SF Compute？再说，你知道，答案会是市场操纵，但让我们真正深入探讨多个参与者的激励因素。

turns.en: Yeah, so our impression is that Nvidia can't make it but benefits tremendously from it existing. The reason why they can't make it is because they would then not be independent enough for people to trade on it. If you don't trade on it, then you don't have enough liquidity for lenders to finance against the forwards market. This is also why Crusoe and Coreweave and Lambda, why the hyperscalers can't make it, why Base10 and Fireworks and Modal can't make it cuz they have too much demand on that side. This is the thing that benefits the entire industry because it makes the financing costs go down. But nobody can make it unless they give up the ability to do all the big inference money and all the big cloud deals. You have to kill your business in order to make this. That's why nobody does it. It's like structurally they're not set up to do that. And you're basically reducing friction and that's all your revenue.
turns.zh: 是的，所以我们的印象是，英伟达无法做到，但从它的存在中获益巨大。他们做不到的原因是他们不够独立，人们无法在上面交易。如果你不在上面交易，那么你就没有足够的流动性让贷款人针对远期市场融资。这也是为什么 Crusoe、Coreweave 和 Lambda，为什么超大规模厂商做不到，为什么 Base10、Fireworks 和 Modal 做不到，因为他们在那一边有太多需求。这是对整个行业有益的事情，因为它降低了融资成本。但没有人能做到，除非他们放弃赚取所有大额推理收入和大额云交易的能力。你必须扼杀你的业务才能做到这一点。这就是为什么没有人做。就像结构上他们不是这样设置的。而你基本上是在减少摩擦，这就是你所有的收入。

turns.en: You've announced some benchmark, some milestones. Actually, I forgot to say that up front. Can you repeat what they are and just take a victory lap a little bit?
turns.zh: 你们宣布了一些基准，一些里程碑。实际上，我忘了在前面说。你能重复一下它们是什么，并稍微炫耀一下吗？

turns.en: We closed several hundred million dollars of volume. We have a significant number of new clusters on the way. And then the things that I think I'm most excited about is we've shipped a whole bunch of new features that make SF Compute very viable for platform as a service companies. An example is we allow customers to subdivide their InfiniBand fabric without having to ask us. So, many clouds when you go to buy them, they will give you one InfiniBand fabric. And then if you want to redraw the lines of that InfiniBand fabric, you need to contact them and they will then do something for you. We now can do that on the fly for customers, which I think is really great because it interfaces with the market really well, where you want to be able to redraw things in order to scale up and down your clusters.
turns.zh: 我们完成了数亿美元的交易量。我们有许多新集群即将到来。然后我认为我最兴奋的事情是我们发布了一大堆新功能，使 SF Compute 对平台即服务公司非常可行。一个例子是我们允许客户细分他们的 InfiniBand 网络结构，而无需询问我们。所以，许多云当你去购买时，他们会给你一个 InfiniBand 网络结构。然后如果你想重新划分那个 InfiniBand 网络结构的线路，你需要联系他们，然后他们会为你做些什么。我们现在可以实时为客户做到这一点，我认为这真的很棒，因为它与市场很好地接口，你希望能够重新划分东西以扩大和缩小你的集群。

turns.en: Would you describe this as like you're virtualizing the data center and making it programmable?
turns.zh: 你会把这描述为你们正在虚拟化数据中心并使其可编程吗？

turns.en: Yeah, we're virtualizing data center and making it programmable. So, all the stuff that you would have gotten if you had owned the hardware, we're trying to virtualize that, which I think is exciting to us.
turns.zh: 是的，我们正在虚拟化数据中心并使其可编程。所以，如果你拥有硬件，你会得到的所有东西，我们正试图虚拟化，我认为这对我们来说很令人兴奋。

turns.en: It's funny like the last time this happened was like the cloud. Like the—Yeah. Which is really cool. And then finally I think what is your call to action for people, you know, is it engineers? Is it like give me your supply? Like what is it?
turns.zh: 有趣的是，上次发生这种情况就像云一样。就像——是的。这真的很酷。然后最后我想你对人们的行动号召是什么，你知道，是工程师吗？是像给我你的供应？像是什么？

turns.en: If you would like to own a GPU cluster and you want the residual value from it, you want to have it for your portfolio, we would love to work with you in order to build that GPU cluster. We will take over and we will do the supercomputing portions of that and ensure the things go right. We own the SLA.
turns.zh: 如果你想拥有一个 GPU 集群，并希望从中获得剩余价值，你想把它纳入你的投资组合，我们很乐意与你合作构建那个 GPU 集群。我们将接管并完成其中的超级计算部分，确保事情顺利进行。我们拥有 SLA。

transcript.secZh: 背板管理与数据中心运营

turns.en: And then if it turns out that that was a bad idea, that you need out of that cluster, we can immediately sell that cluster to someone else so it doesn't hit your balance sheet.
turns.zh: 然后如果事实证明那是个坏主意、你需要退出那个集群，我们可以立刻把那个集群卖给别人，这样就不会冲击你的资产负债表。

turns.en: Very simple pitch. Well, thank you so much for your time. You're doing a great service to the industry, and I just am happy to be your friend.
turns.zh: 非常简单的推介。好了，非常感谢你抽出时间。你在为这个行业做很大的贡献，我很高兴能成为你的朋友。

turns.en: I appreciate it.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: All right. That's it.
turns.zh: 好的，就到这里。
